clue.text: Hated to move on to improvised way of settling match

indicators.note: the second piece is placed on to the end of the first

parts.note: something improvised is unplanned, sprung without warning, so sudden

indicators.note: the letters of the word are made to move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having to switch to an ad-libbed method of deciding a tied game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges HATED into DEATH, which goes 'on to' SUDDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreak format in which the first score wins the drawn fixture outright.

clue.text: Cast assuring silence for leading actor

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so these letters are thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A director's casting choice promises quiet on set for the star of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the theatrical noun, but it is the signal to rearrange ASSURING SILENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous British star of film and stage, a prime example of a top performer.

clue.text: Pictured as tense

definitions.meaning: sketched in pencil or ink, depicted
strained and haggard, as of a worried face

explanation.surface: Someone is shown in a picture looking anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of the verb for sketching, and also an adjective for a strained, haggard look.

clue.text: From one direction, point to the back of the ship

parts.note: E is east, one of the compass points

parts.words: to the back of the ship
parts.note: astern means towards the rear of a vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor indicates the rear of the vessel, giving a bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from the sunrise side, one particular compass bearing.

clue.text: Long for European girl

parts.note: to long for something is to desire it

explanation.surface: Someone pines for a young woman from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a crossword stand-in for any girl.

clue.text: Worried by area — see it secured all round

indicators.note: the secured word wraps all round the little word it, enclosing it

parts.note: a gated place is shut off and made secure

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a district, urged to check it has been fenced off on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is only a link word here, pointing at what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe a person who is anxious and flustered.

clue.text: They have you going in circles around the airport

definitions.text: They have you going in circles around the airport

parts.words: They have you going in circles around the airport
parts.note: planes waiting to land are made to fly loops over the airfield; the surface hints at confusing terminal signage

explanation.surface: Something at an airport keeps leaving travellers lost and walking in loops.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacked circuits flown by aircraft awaiting clearance to land.

clue.text: Cutlery and a set of plates one may have at a banquet

definitions.text: one may have at a banquet

parts.note: silver is a name for knives, forks and spoons
a dinner service is a matching set of crockery

explanation.surface: Knives, forks and a matching dinner set laid out for a grand feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal style of waiting in which food is served from platters at table, typical of grand dinners.

clue.text: The latest is the responsibility of very small people

parts.note: a job is up to someone when it is theirs to do
minute means tiny, so the minute are read as the tiny folk

explanation.surface: A whimsical claim that keeping current is a task for little folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being completely current, the most recent version.

clue.text: These incursions not cross-country?

definitions.meaning: advances made into enemy territory or a market
travelling on the highways rather than over open fields

explanation.surface: Raids that keep to the tarmac rather than the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances that intrude on territory are the standard idiom for encroachments.

clue.text: Boards' arrangement of vessel to drink

parts.note: a ship is a seagoing vessel
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A boat's planks laid out so that the vessel takes in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber cladding in which planks are fitted edge to edge or overlapping.

clue.text: One can't be forced to work

definitions.text: One can't be forced to work

parts.words: One can't be forced to work
parts.note: someone who offers labour freely, unpaid and by choice; the surface sounds like a complaint about a broken machine

explanation.surface: Sounds like a gadget that simply will not function however hard it is pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person offering their labour freely is by definition not conscripted.

clue.text: A fighter's old friend

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A boxer's longtime pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for pal, borrowed into English for a mate.

clue.text: Could it make a lamb joint stretch?

definitions.text: Could it make a lamb joint
definitions.meaning: a cut of ribs roasted as a joint of lamb
to pull on a torture frame, or strain

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some cut could be pulled out into a joint of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib roast of lamb, and the medieval torture frame that stretches its victim.

clue.text: Such as would suit you down to the ground? Only half

definitions.text: Such as would suit you down to the ground? Only half

parts.words: Such as would suit you down to the ground? Only half
parts.note: a garment that reaches the ground is floor-length; one going only half that way stops at the joint mid-leg

explanation.surface: Something is perfectly suitable, but only partly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit you down to the ground' means suit perfectly, but here it is a skirt or coat literally reaching the floor; halve that and it stops mid-leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a skirt or coat whose hem stops at the joint midway down the leg.

clue.text: Something for tea brought by pack mule

indicators.note: the letters are brought along jumbled up, delivered in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A treat for afternoon tea carried up by a beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit-laden sponge, a classic thing served at teatime.

clue.text: Evening game

parts.note: making the score level in a match; the surface suggests a match played after dark

explanation.surface: A match played at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' reads as the time of day but means making even.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring to bring the sides level is the act of making a contest even.

clue.text: Most peevish, so you say 'relax'

indicators.note: say marks that the word before it is to be spoken, giving its sound as a letter

parts.note: the word you, spoken, is the letter U
to relax is to rest

explanation.surface: A grumpy reply: so you are telling me to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' gives U, the letter that sounds like 'you', between SO and REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of an adjective for bad-tempered and embittered.

clue.text: Two presents can't be found?

parts.note: two senses of present, at this moment and in this place, joined to give a word for absent from every place

explanation.surface: A pair of gifts has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' is not gifts but the adjective present, in time and in place; the two words joined mean in no place at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absent from every location is said to be not anywhere at all.

clue.text: Conflict taking month to heat up

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: Hostilities take a month to really flare up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise the temperature of something.

clue.text: A bit of love, no more malice

indicators.note: only a portion of the words is taken, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Affection gone, only spite remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and bitter ill will, figuratively poison.

clue.text: Sort of rule you can't look up?

definitions.text: Sort of rule you can't look up?

parts.words: Sort of rule you can't look up?
parts.note: a convention never set down on paper, so there is no book to check it in

explanation.surface: A regulation absent from any reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tacit convention, understood by all but never recorded on paper.

clue.text: Be liable for where a dog's dinner's gone?

parts.note: the food has gone in, eaten
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Taking the blame for the state of a messy meal fed to the pet.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's dinner is British slang for a mess, but here the dinner has gone in a cur.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a cost or penalty on oneself is to become liable for it.

clue.text: Make a fuss about mass way to dispose of bodies

indicators.note: the fuss word goes about the mass letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to create is to make a fuss or scene

explanation.surface: Kicking up a stink over a cheap mass method of handling the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce corpses to ashes by burning is a method of dealing with remains.

clue.text: It's only a tiny bit of work

definitions.text: It's only a tiny bit of work

parts.words: It's only a tiny bit of work
parts.note: a short passage taken from a book or piece of music; the surface sounds like a modest job

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a job as barely any effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extract quoted from a longer written or musical piece.

clue.text: Lovers share tweets when travelling

indicators.note: letters on the move shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Couples post messages to each other while on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: affectionate partners in a romance.
